items.claim: I could use Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz, Tiefgarage Friedensplatz, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim, and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus.
items.reason: These are the four usable parking series in August 2026.

items.claim: On weekdays, these four lots together were quietest at 03:00 and busiest at 11:00.
items.reason: The pooled weekday profile is quietest at 03:00 and busiest at 12:00, not 11:00.

items.claim: The clearest weekday pattern was at Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus, which was often between 74.0% and 87.2% in the late morning and around midday, while Tiefgarage Friedensplatz stayed very low overnight, often between 2.2% and 11.4%.
items.reason: Ulrichshaus has the highest r_squared, but FACTS do not contain the quoted ranges; its weekday peak is 72.5% and Friedensplatz's overnight trough is 6.3%.

items.claim: Weekend and weekday use were clearly different, but not in the same way everywhere.
items.reason: The pooled test is significant and the weekend effect differs across lots.

items.claim: Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz was fuller at weekends, especially later in the day.
items.reason: FACTS support fuller weekends overall, but not that the effect was especially later in the day.

items.claim: It reached 86.7% on 8 August at 22:00, 100.0% on 15 August at 21:00, and 88.1% on 30 August at 19:00.
items.reason: FACTS only give aggregate summaries and do not contain the dated occupancies 86.7% or 88.1% or those timestamps.

items.claim: On many weekdays at the same part of the day it stayed much lower.
items.reason: FACTS show weekdays were lower than weekends overall, but not how often that happened in that part of the day.

items.claim: Tiefgarage Friedensplatz and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus showed the opposite pattern, with fuller weekday middays than weekend middays.
items.reason: Both lots peak around midday on weekdays and have significant negative weekend effects.

items.claim: Compared with July, Tiefgarage Hotel Maritim was fuller overall in August, while Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz was emptier overall.
items.reason: Hotel Maritim was significantly fuller, but Elbauenpark - Messeparkplatz showed no significant month-to-month change.

items.claim: At Tiefgarage Friedensplatz and Tiefgarage Ulrichshaus, I did not see a clear month-to-month change.
items.reason: Both adjusted shifts are not significant.

items.claim: I used 18 stations.
items.reason: FACTS say there are 18 stations in total, but only 15 were usable and 3 were excluded.

items.claim: The weekday charging pattern was broad rather than sharp.
items.reason: FACTS give the weekday profile but do not define or measure whether it is 'broad rather than sharp'.

items.claim: Use was usually quietest in the small hours, built up after 08:00, stayed busiest from late morning into early evening, and then eased again after 20:00.
items.reason: The median weekday profile bottoms out at 04:00, rises after 08:00, stays highest around late morning through evening, and declines after 20:00.

items.claim: A few stations stayed busy for long stretches, especially Breiter Weg 203, Hegelstraße 4, and Julius-Bremer-Straße 1, which often sat at 50.0% to 100.0% for several hours in a row.
items.reason: FACTS show peaks of 57.6%, 60.1%, and 60.9% and maxima of 100.0%, but do not report 50.0% or 'several hours in a row'.

items.claim: I did not see one clear weekend-weekday split across the whole charging network.
items.reason: The pooled test says weekend effects differ between stations, and individual stations show both positive and negative weekend effects.

items.claim: Some stations were busier on weekend afternoons, while others stayed steadier on weekdays.
items.reason: FACTS report overall weekend effects by station, not afternoon-specific behavior, and they do not describe stations as 'steadier on weekdays'.

items.claim: Compared with July, I did not see a clear citywide change in charging occupancy.
items.reason: The month-on-month summary is mixed: one station is significantly higher, one significantly lower, and eleven show no significant change.

items.claim: I could use all 4 NO2 sites and O3 West.
items.reason: All 4 NO2 sites were usable, and the only usable O3 site was West.

items.claim: At the traffic-oriented NO2 sites, weekdays were usually more polluted than weekends through most daytime hours.
items.reason: City Tunnel and Guericke Strasse have significant negative weekend effects, but Schleinufer's weekend effect is -2.0 µg/m³ and not significant.

items.claim: The clearest pattern was at City Tunnel, Guericke Strasse, and Schleinufer, where values rose after 07:00 and often again from late afternoon into the evening.
items.reason: FACTS give peak hours of 22:00, 09:00, and 23:00 for those sites but not hourly profiles to verify rises after 07:00 and again later.

items.claim: West stayed much lower than those three sites through the month.
items.reason: West's mean NO2 was 6.9 µg/m³ versus 26.7, 17.1, and 18.3 at the other three sites.

items.claim: I saw no NO2 hourly breach of the EU limit of 200 µg/m³.
items.reason: All four NO2 sites had 0 hours over the EU hourly limit of 200 µg/m³.

items.claim: Daily means still went above the WHO 25 µg/m³ guideline on some days at City Tunnel, Schleinufer, and Guericke Strasse, but not at West.
items.reason: WHO daily-guideline exceedance days were 17 at City Tunnel, 3 at Schleinufer, 3 at Guericke Strasse, and 0 at West.

items.claim: For ozone, the pattern was the reverse.
items.reason: O3 West peaks at 18:00, but its weekend effect is -2.2 µg/m³ and not significant, so FACTS do not show a simple reverse of NO2.

items.claim: O3 West was usually highest in the afternoon and evening, and weekend afternoons were often higher than weekday afternoons.
items.reason: West's O3 peak hour is 18:00, but its weekend effect is -2.2 µg/m³ and not significant.

items.claim: The highest hourly value was 173.0 µg/m³ at 17:00 on 15 August.
items.reason: FACTS confirm a max of 173.0 µg/m³ but do not give the hourly-maximum timestamp; the only 15 August time shown is the 8-hour worst_when at 00:00.

items.claim: The 8-hour ozone value went above the WHO 100 µg/m³ guideline on 9 days and above the EU 120 µg/m³ target on 5 days.
items.reason: FACTS say 15 WHO-guideline exceedance days and 7 EU-target exceedance days.

items.claim: That was more than in July, when I saw 5 WHO exceedance days and no EU-target exceedance day.
items.reason: FACTS include August ozone exceedance counts only, not July exceedance-day counts.

items.claim: I did not describe particulate pollution this month, because the particle sensors were not reliable enough.
items.reason: FACTS say all PM10 and PM2.5 series were excluded as stale, not that the sensors were generally 'not reliable enough'.
